title: GULP: building a playable 3D monster arena with Codex, Claude and generated assets
author: itxpratik
selftext:
I’m making GULP for a Monster Mash jam. It’s a browser arena: eat food and villagers, grow, gulp smaller monsters and escape bigger ones. Growth also slows you down, so getting huge has a cost.



My workflow has been to use RUN for generated monster/art assets, Codex and Claude for coding assistance, and Three.js for the game. The city also uses Kenney models. This is a mix of generated assets and an existing asset library, not a fully generated world.



The first playable version wasn’t the end of the work. I’ve been iterating on collision problems, empty parts of the city, mobile HUD space and Android performance. The UI also took several passes: a nice cover image can still place the character under the Play button or leave the wrong space for controls. Keeping that composition constraint explicit was important.



The current version has online/solo play, three-minute rounds, unlockable skins and global leaderboards. I’d like feedback on the actual game feel, especially whether getting larger feels rewarding without removing the smaller monster’s chance to escape.



Play: [https://w.run/pratikmane/gulp?s=EPVt3Ru](https://w.run/pratikmane/gulp?s=EPVt3Ru)

Actual solo gameplay clip: [https://youtu.be/2OIMIByzU0g](https://youtu.be/2OIMIByzU0g)



How do you keep generated characters and library environment assets visually consistent while staying within a mobile rendering budget?
